verbs.text: Groaned under the weight of the food
Steamed in the middle of the table

sentences.text: The whole family gathered for Sunday lunch at the long, polished table.
He spread a crisp, starched tablecloth and laid out the cutlery with a ruler's precision.
Dad carved the roast while Mum passed the potatoes.
She took the jug of thick, brown gravy and poured it over everything.
Tall, white candles flickered in the candlesticks.
Delicate crystal glasses glittered in the candlelight.
The guests clinked their glasses and wished one another a happy new year.
Chairs scraped on the floor as everyone sat down.
High-backed wooden chairs stood stiffly along each side, like guests who had arrived too early.
The cousins chattered and laughed at the raucous, crowded table.
The children tucked in hungrily and heaped their plates high.
The table groaned under the weight of the food.
An enormous, golden roast turkey steamed in the middle of the table.
They ate in silence in the gloomy, chilly dining room, every scrape of a fork too loud.
The glass tipped, and a dark stain spread across the tablecloth.
By the end of the party, the sticky, stained tablecloth was a map of the whole meal.
They cleared away the dishes, carrying the fine bone china with exaggerated care.
The latecomers squeezed in at the end, on odd, mismatched chairs.
The grown-ups lingered over their coffee in the warm, convivial room.
The heavy, oak sideboard was full of china that had stood unused for years.
They scraped their plates clean and asked for more.
The grand, candlelit dining room glowed with gold and silver.
Gleaming silver cutlery lay beside every plate, in strict order of use.
Steaming dishes of vegetables were carried in from the kitchen.
A cold, congealed meal sat at the head of the long, deserted table.
Neatly folded napkins stood on each plate like small white sails.
The window blew open, and the wind snuffed out the candles and sent napkins flying.
Nobody dared to speak while Grandfather glared down the length of the table.
Rain pattered on the windows, but inside the room was warm and smelled of roast potatoes.
She ate alone every evening, with only the ticking clock for company.
